---
title: "Unmatched rows, stacking and comparing data cuts"
description: >
  Open the rows behind a check count as a card, stack tables with a check, and compare two cuts of a table by key.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(sideview)
```

A check on the canvas gives you counts. A **derived card** gives you the rows behind them, as a card of its own,
with code that rebuilds it. Everything below uses small synthetic tables built in the page (no real patients).

## Rows behind a count

A join check or a SUPP check offers buttons that open the rows behind its counts: the rows of either table with no
match, the rows a date rule dropped, and the SUPP rows with no parent row or with an `IDVARVAL` that does not
convert. The card is named for what it holds (`ae_unmatched_dm`) and is built by R from the tables as loaded, so a
duckdb or Arrow input stays lazy. From the console, `sv_unmatched()` and `sv_supp_orphans()` return the same rows.

```{r unmatched}
dm <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S-01", "S-02", "S-03"), AGE = c(34, 51, 62))
ae <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S-01", "S-02", "S-09"), AESEQ = 1L,
                 AETERM = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Rash"))
sv_unmatched(ae, dm, by = "USUBJID")
```

```{r unmatched-gadget, eval = FALSE}
sideview(dm, ae)   # connect USUBJID to USUBJID, then use the buttons on the join check
```

## Stacking tables

`sv_stack_check()` lines up the columns of 2 to 8 tables and reports, per column, its type in each table and what a
stack would do: the same type, a cast to a common type, a name that differs only by case offered as a rename, and a
column missing from some tables. Nothing changes until you pick a fix. `sv_stack()` stacks the tables with the
check's fixes, adds a `source` column naming each row's table, and turns a value that cannot be cast into `NA`.

```{r stack}
wave1 <- data.frame(ID = 1:2, AGE = c(40L, 52L))
wave2 <- data.frame(ID = 3:4, Age = c(61, 47))
chk <- sv_stack_check(wave1 = wave1, wave2 = wave2)
sv_stack(wave1 = wave1, wave2 = wave2, check = chk)
```

In the gadget, the drawer has a **Stack** tab: pick tables, Check, change a fix, and **Open** adds the stacked
table as a card.

## Comparing data cuts

`sv_compare(old, new, by)` matches the rows of two cuts of a table on a key and counts the rows **added** (key only
in `new`), **removed** (key only in `old`) and **changed** (key in both, a value differs). It also lists columns that
were added, removed or changed type, and the changed values by column. Nothing is modified.

```{r compare-data}
ae_old <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S-01", "S-02", "S-03", "S-04"), AESEQ = 1L,
                     AETERM = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Rash", "Cough"),
                     AESEV = c("MILD", "MODERATE", "MILD", "SEVERE"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ae_new <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S-01", "S-02", "S-04", "S-05"), AESEQ = 1L,
                     AETERM = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Cough", "Dizziness"),
                     AESEV = c("MILD", "SEVERE", "SEVERE", "MILD"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

```{r compare}
sv_compare(ae_old, ae_new, by = c("USUBJID", "AESEQ"))
```

Here `S-05` is new, `S-03` is gone, and `S-02` changed severity. In the gadget, the drawer's **Compare** tab does
the same: pick the old and the new table, Check, change the key if the suggestion is wrong (with no key picked, a
CDISC tag suggests one), and **Open** each set of rows as a card: `ae_new_added`, `ae_old_removed` and
`ae_new_changed` (the changed rows carry the old and new value side by side). Each card is one `derive` step whose R
code is plain `dplyr`, and a duckdb or Arrow input stays lazy.

```{r compare-gadget, eval = FALSE}
sideview(ae_old, ae_new)   # open the drawer, choose the Compare tab
```

The widget has no R, so it has no Compare tab; a saved compare step stays in the code, with a notice that the table
is not shown.
